chunks.title: Conferences Sumit has attended
chunks.text:
Conferences Sumit has attended
- PyTorch Conference North America 2026 (Silicon Valley): Sumit attended on a PyTorch community scholarship and met the researchers and engineers building the framework. Highlights included dinner with the AWS Trainium team talking about AI accelerators, and visits to Google and NVIDIA headquarters.
- 105th Annual Mathematical Association of America (MAA) Regional Conference at Baylor University (2026): Sumit represented Texas State University in the MAA Math Bowl with TXST professors and teammates, and the team placed second runner-up out of 25 teams.
- Texas State University undergraduate research conference: Sumit presented a research poster on adversarial robustness using optimal transport-based models.

chunks.section: Experience: Machine Learning Engineering Intern at Microsoft
chunks.title: Experience: Machine Learning Engineering Intern at Microsoft
chunks.text:
Experience: Machine Learning Engineering Intern at Microsoft
Microsoft Corporation, ODSP-DEEDS team, Redmond, WA. May 2026 – Aug 2026.
- Developed and evaluated vectorless RAG pipelines (retrieval without dense embeddings), including LLM-Wiki and PageIndex, in offline experiments benchmarking retrieval approaches for enterprise-scale content grounding in Microsoft Copilot.
- Conducted recall-focused experiments across query sets and retrieval configurations, increasing Recall@K from a 68% baseline to as high as 96% with the best-performing approach.
- Built an LLM-as-a-judge evaluation pipeline using assertion-based checklists to assess generated responses, achieving 100% completeness and up to 89% response quality on targeted evaluation sets.
- Explored LLM-based query generation, reformulation, and container summarization to improve semantic search coverage across complex document hierarchies.

chunks.section: Experience: Undergraduate Research Assistant at Texas State University
chunks.title: Experience: Undergraduate Research Assistant at Texas State University
chunks.text:
Experience: Undergraduate Research Assistant at Texas State University
Department of Mathematics & Computer Science, Texas State University, San Marcos, TX. Apr 2025 – Present.
- Conducted research on optimal transport-based distributionally robust optimization (OT-DRO) for robust regression, benchmarking against OLS, ridge, and lasso under noise, outliers, distribution shift, and sparsity settings using Python and PyTorch.
- Presented research findings through conference poster presentations and invited departmental talks, communicating theoretical insights and experimental results on robust regression and optimal transport to academic audiences.

chunks.title: Project: AI-Powered Study Assistant
chunks.text:
Project: AI-Powered Study Assistant
Tech: React, Flask, Firebase, OpenAI API, Qdrant. GitHub: https://github.com/sumit-sah314/ai-study-tool-repository
- Built an AI-powered study platform that generates quizzes from course notes, identifies weak topics, and tracks learning progress through personalized study workflows.
- Designed a semantic retrieval pipeline with Qdrant vector search to surface relevant course-note context before OpenAI-powered quiz generation.
- Implemented real-time Firestore synchronization and unit tests for quiz tracking, history retrieval, answer review, and retake workflows.
